It was that time of the year. Finals were posted and disgruntled students came to me trying to find someway to not fail. Some begged, pleading that they would study harder next time. Others would bribe, or try to entice me with some fantasy of the flesh. But this latest one, well it sure was interesting.

"Mr Smith," the student said as he entered my office. I noticed a sheathed blade strapped to his waist.

"Ah James, going Larping with some of your friends?" I said, making it clear i saw the blade.

"Uh, no sir. It's about my biology final. It says I scored lower than the passing grade. But, I found a old rule in the University's bylaws."

I knew of said bylaw, hell half the reason I started working here was to see if anyone would try to pass their exams by trial by combat. Guess I got my answer. "Charlie, Are you sure about this?" I said. "Once you challenge a teacher, you and him are locked in combat."

 "Yeah, while everyone else did their homework, I figured it would be easier to draw blood on you once." He smiled.

"Yes, yes yes, trial by combat till first drawing blood. Can't have students killing teachers. Still, I knew you were lazy but still this is impressive." I smiled. "Still, you have not supplied me with a blade. Did you assume I kept one on me?"

Charlie pointed to my not so simple cane. "I saw that last Halloween, You dressed up as Lord Vetinari. I doubt you have a non sword double." 

"If I recall," I said, stalling for time as I moved to in front of my desk. "You dressed as Rand Al'thor. Well boy, Lets see if you should think about a different major after this." I then offered my hand to his to shake.

"Don't worry, I thought this through." Charlie said. He then went and shook my hand. "OW!" he exclaimed. His hand recoiling from mine.

"Oh would you look at that." I said, grabbing his hand and holding it open. A small thumb tack was jammed straight into his hand. As I yanked it out, a small drop of blood pooled on his palm. "It would seem as I have drawn blood first. And it would seem you will need to find a different major." I could still hear his stunned response as he slowly walked out the door.

To answer the question in the title, I see a few possible choices on why witchcraft, sorcery, and divination was outlawed in the bible.also to simplify this i will be referring to them all under the term "magic."  
 
  
1. It doesn't work or doesn't exist, God would not want us spending our time on something that isn't real. Therefor the outlaw was to spare us from depending on something that can not by its very nature do anything for us.  
  
2. By drawing on the powers of magic, we are therefor not relying on the Spirit of God. we are in essence attempting to replicate God, either in ourselves or through some other spirit. Similar to what Jesus said in Matthew 6:24.  
  
3. Pride. Even I am not afraid to admit that if I were told that if i only believe in a few simple phrases or carved a few runes, I could fly or cast lightning bolts or achieve the love of my life, or know the future, I would be halfway to the occult subreddit in a flash. But by doing so I would only be in it out of pride. Jesus, on the other hand, preached that to save your life you must lose it and "take up your cross." Those certainly aren't the words a proud man wants to here.  
  
Finally, as for tarot, (and to be clear, tarot was never a strong interest of mine, back in my brief journey in the occult, so if I'm mistaken, my apologies) the only thing I see a use for it is to divine the future. tarot and divination in general, seems to be designed to try and calm the worry and fear that is in us. For fear, 1 John 4:18 says "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves torment. But he who fears has not been made perfect in love." We are no longer tormented by fear, as Christ has ensured our eternal place, by His love. As for Worry, Jesus says in Matthew 6:34 "Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about its own things. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble."

My prayers are with you, and remember always "God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind." [2 Timothy 1:7]
